main_text.p: rum genere,quæ plurimū calefaciunt, siue alexyteria sint, siue quælibet alia, quæ suis qualitatibus manifestis uim alterandi ha-bent,cauendum esse,rationi cōsentaneum[?] est. Huiusmodi autem vulgata sunt hæc, nempe zedoaria,myrrha, radix cucumeris agrestis,allium,cepa,ruta,polium,calamintha, abrotonum,origanum,tetragoriganum, radices angelicæ,imperatoriæ,& alia id genus simplicia,quorum acrimonia, quatam[?] uim nostra calefaciendi corpora habeant, satis declarat. Horum numero etiam ascri-bi debet illa theriacalis aqua,quę illo tem-pore,quo sæuisima pestis Lugduni tan-topere grassabatur,à quoda Germano me-dico,cui Stapedius nomen erat, auro char-rior uenalis prostabat. Quamuis enim eam theriaca ingrediatur, quæ uenenis resistit, nihilominus tamen ob ardentem aquam, quā sufflones fumivori aquam vitę, & vini spiritum uocant, & in qua dissoluitur ipsa theriaca, humanum corpus impense accendit:propterea ipsum pestilenti febri magis reddit obnoxium. Adde quòd si morbo ipso iam correptis propinetur multa, peste ma-gis magisq; accendet,eamq; exitiosiorem efficiet : propterea quòd tum spiritus, tum humores

page.notes: Catchword "humores" at lower right, kept out of the text. Page opens mid-sentence, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". Doubtful readings: "cōsentaneum" (long s makes it look like "cofentaneum"), "quatam" (probably quædam), and "charior" (line break "cha-/rior" with "rior uenalis" printed without a space). The printed "dit:propterea" and "efficiet :" are kept as printed. Long s is normalised to plain s throughout.
